exampleDiagnoses.example: The startup culture that worships founders as visionaries often overlooks the contributions of the entire team.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 批判视角——worship让人选择性失明。

exampleDiagnoses.example: He goes to worship every morning before dawn — it's not about religion, he says, it's about silence.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 精神修行——worship可以被重新定义。

synonymComparisons.difference: 崇拜/敬拜（宗教+世俗极度崇拜）
synonymComparisons.example: He worshipped his wife like a goddess.

synonymComparisons.difference: 非常喜爱（温柔/亲昵的崇拜）
synonymComparisons.example: She adores her grandchildren beyond words.

synonymComparisons.difference: 偶像化/过度崇拜（把凡人神化）
synonymComparisons.example: Teenagers tend to idolize pop stars unrealistically.

synonymComparisons.difference: 深深尊敬（庄重/不盲目的敬意）
synonymComparisons.example: Nelson Mandela is revered around the world for his humanity.

oneLinePenetration: worship是"你认为什么最大"的外在表现——你worship什么，你就是什么样的人。你跪在谁的面前，你的世界就以谁为中心旋转。

posNote: 值得的；有意义的；划算的

forms.note: 值得的；有意义的；划算的

coreImage: 周末你去当了八小时志愿者——搬砖、扫地、送盒饭，回到家腰酸背痛，但你笑了，你觉得这一天没白过。worthwhile就是那个"你投入了时间/精力/金钱，然后回头看，觉得值"的时刻。不是赚了多少，而是你愿意再做一次。worthwhile的前提是有付出——爬山的人知道，只有爬上去的人才有资格说"值得"。

semanticRadii.label: 有价值的结果
semanticRadii.example: What makes all the late nights worthwhile is seeing students actually "get it".

semanticRadii.label: 经济上合算
semanticRadii.example: The repairs were expensive, but the increase in home value made it worthwhile.

grammarRules.title: 用法说明
items: 形容词：a worthwhile cause/experience/investment/effort/activity。it作形式主语：It is worthwhile to do sth / doing sth。make sth worthwhile（让...有价值）。find sth worthwhile（发现...值得做）。be well worthwhile（非常值得）。注意拼写：worth + while（worth your while），常见错误worthwild/manwhile。

exampleDiagnoses.example: She spent years studying a field that didn't pay well, but she never doubted it was worthwhile.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 价值观——worthwhile不总等于高薪。

exampleDiagnoses.example: The hardest thing about teaching is that you may never know if you made a difference — but you trust the effort is worthwhile.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 信念——有些worthwhile没有即时回执。

synonymComparisons.difference: 值得花时间/精力做（投入产出正）
synonymComparisons.example: It's a difficult climb but absolutely worthwhile.

synonymComparisons.difference: 有价值的/宝贵的（客观价值高）
synonymComparisons.example: This is a valuable painting — worth millions.

synonymComparisons.difference: 有回报的/让人满足的（情感体验好）
synonymComparisons.example: Working with children is incredibly rewarding.

synonymComparisons.difference: 值...（后接名词/动名词/金钱）
synonymComparisons.example: This book is worth reading. It costs $10 — worth every penny.

oneLinePenetration: worthwhile是"worth your while"——你的生命被花在了它应该被花的地方。你弯腰捡贝壳，别人觉得你浪费时间，但你手里有海的形状，那就是worthwhile。

posNote: 残骸；严重受损的人/物/船

forms.note: 残骸；严重受损的人/物/船

coreImage: 一艘巨轮撞上礁石，船体从中断裂，海浪把碎片冲上岸——木板、货物、人的杂物散落一滩。wreck就是被毁灭后的样子：船wreck，车wreck，婚姻wreck，一个人喝醉了一塌糊涂也叫wreck。它不是轻微损坏，是"彻底垮掉、不成样子"。作动词时，wreck是摧毁——一个下午可以wreck你准备了半年的计划，一句话可以wreck一段多年的感情。

semanticRadii.label: 车祸/空难
semanticRadii.example: The wreck was so severe that the car was unrecognizable.

semanticRadii.label: 精神崩溃
semanticRadii.example: After the custody battle, she was a nervous wreck for months.

semanticRadii.label: 彻底毁坏
semanticRadii.example: One reckless decision wrecked his entire career.

grammarRules.title: 用法说明
items: 名词：the wreck of a ship/car，a train wreck（也比喻灾难性失败），a nervous wreck（精神崩溃的人），be a complete/total wreck。动词：wreck sth（完全毁坏），wreck relationships/plans/hopes/chances/health。形容词wrecked：I am wrecked（极度疲惫，口语）。

exampleDiagnoses.example: He walked away from the car wreck without a scratch — physically. But the memory wrecked something inside him.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 双重叙事——物理wreck vs 心理wreck。

exampleDiagnoses.example: Their financial mismanagement wrecked the company beyond repair, leaving hundreds without jobs.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 商业灾难——wreck作动词是毁灭性的大范围打击。

synonymComparisons.difference: 严重毁坏/残骸（残破到难以修复）
synonymComparisons.example: The scandal wrecked his political career.

synonymComparisons.difference: 摧毁/消灭（完全破坏，抽象/具体均可）
synonymComparisons.example: The fire destroyed the entire building.

synonymComparisons.difference: 毁坏/糟蹋（常指不可逆的美/价值的损失）
synonymComparisons.example: The graffiti ruined the historic monument.

synonymComparisons.difference: 拆除（有计划地/用机械地拆掉建筑）
synonymComparisons.example: They plan to demolish the old stadium next month.

oneLinePenetration: wreck的震撼在于"之前还是完整的，之后就不成样子了"。更可怕的是——修复永远比毁坏难一万倍。那个wreck的船骸会躺在海底三百年，而撞上礁石只需要三秒钟。

coreImage: 你用尽全力把一个生锈的螺栓拧开——肌肉绷紧，脸涨红，突然"啪"一声，螺栓松了。wrench就是那种"用蛮力突然扭转或拉扯"的动作。它也可以是情感上的——"把某人从某人身边硬拽走"，那种撕裂感。wrench还有一个意思：扳手，就是用来wrench的工具。物理上wrench是力的爆发，情感上wrench是心的撕裂。

semanticRadii.label: 扭伤关节
semanticRadii.example: She wrenched her ankle on the hiking trail and had to be carried back.

semanticRadii.label: 强行夺走
semanticRadii.structure: wrench sth from sb, wrench sb away
semanticRadii.meaning: 从某人手里抢走/把某人拽走
semanticRadii.example: The child was wrenched from his mother's arms by the social workers.

semanticRadii.label: 令人悲痛
semanticRadii.example: The documentary was a heart-wrenching account of the refugee crisis.

semanticRadii.label: 扳手
semanticRadii.example: Hand me the wrench — I need to loosen this pipe.

grammarRules.title: 用法说明
items: 动词：wrench sth + adj（wrench the door open），wrench sth from/out of sb（夺走/抢走），wrench oneself free（挣脱）。wrench one's ankle/knee（扭伤）。名词：give sth a wrench（猛扭一下）。形容词：heart-wrenching（撕心裂肺的），gut-wrenching（让人反胃/精神痛苦的）。工具：monkey wrench, adjustable wrench。

exampleDiagnoses.example: Watching her son leave for war felt like a physical wrench — as if part of her body was being torn away.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 情感撕裂——wrench作名词描述被硬生生挖走一块的感觉。

exampleDiagnoses.example: The plumber gave the rusty pipe a quick wrench and it finally came loose.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 工具和动作合一——wrench既是名词也是动词，扳手做wrench的动作。

synonymComparisons.difference: 猛力扭/拉（力量+突然性+疼痛）
synonymComparisons.example: She wrenched the bag out of the thief's hand.

synonymComparisons.difference: 旋转/扭曲（不一定暴力，可轻柔）
synonymComparisons.example: Twist the lid clockwise to open.

synonymComparisons.difference: 扭伤（医学用语，专指韧带损伤）
synonymComparisons.example: He sprained his wrist playing basketball.

synonymComparisons.difference: 猛然拉拽（突然+不规则，非旋转）
synonymComparisons.example: The train jerked forward and she lost her balance.

oneLinePenetration: wrench就是"把你的世界突然拧一下"——可能是你的手腕，可能是你的心，也可能是你手里的扳手。不管是哪一种，都是暴力的、突然的、疼的。

coreImage: 狄更斯小说里那个在雨里发抖的孤儿——浑身湿透，衣服破烂，没人看他一眼。wretched是"惨到让人不忍看"——不只是不幸，是从内到外的惨。它形容人的悲惨处境、极端糟糕的天气、差到令人愤怒的质量、对自己良心的深深厌恶。wretched是"在所有维度上都很糟"——身体、精神、环境，没有一处是好的。

semanticRadii.label: 极度痛苦
semanticRadii.example: She felt wretched about the way she had spoken to her mother.

semanticRadii.label: 恶劣天气/环境
semanticRadii.example: We spent a wretched weekend trapped in the cabin by the storm.

semanticRadii.label: 非常糟糕的
semanticRadii.meaning: 糟糕透顶的失败/表现/质量
semanticRadii.example: The movie was a wretched attempt to capitalize on nostalgia.

grammarRules.title: 用法说明
items: adj.：wretched + 名词（wretched conditions/weather/life/hovel），feel wretched（感到痛苦/不适/内疚）。wretch（n.）可怜虫/坏蛋：you poor wretch!, the ungrateful wretch!。wretchedly adv.：wretchedly poor/unhappy。注意发音：wretched读/ˈretʃ.ɪd/（两个音节），不要读成/retʃt/。

exampleDiagnoses.example: He felt utterly wretched when he realized his careless words had destroyed a lifelong friendship.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 深深内疚——wretched是道德层面的自我厌恶。

exampleDiagnoses.example: The internet connection was so wretched that streaming a two-minute video took an hour.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 日常吐槽——wretched也可以降级使用来描述"糟到令人绝望"的小事。

synonymComparisons.difference: 从内到外都很惨（身体+灵魂+环境）
synonymComparisons.example: The dog looked wretched, thin and trembling in the alley.

synonymComparisons.difference: 痛苦/不快乐的（侧重主观感受）
synonymComparisons.example: He's been miserable ever since he lost his job.

synonymComparisons.difference: 可怜的/可悲的（带轻蔑/施舍感）
synonymComparisons.example: His pathetic excuses fooled no one.

synonymComparisons.difference: 极端/完全的（常与poverty/misery/failure连用）
synonymComparisons.example: They live in abject poverty, without even basic sanitation.

oneLinePenetration: wretched是"惨"的终极形态——不是某一方面不好，是方方面面都不好，而且你改变不了。看着别人wretched你会心软，觉得自己wretched你会心碎。

forms.note: 渴望；思念（yearn for sth / yearn to do sth）

coreImage: 夜深人静，你望着窗外，心里有一种说不清的空。不是缺什么东西，而是一种对远方、对某种生活状态的深切向往。yearning不是饿了想吃饭的生理冲动，是灵魂的饥饿——你知道有某种完整性在别处，而此刻的你不完整。yearn的语气里没有焦躁，它是一种安静的、持续的引力，像一个微弱但永不熄灭的信号。

semanticRadii.label: 思念/乡愁
semanticRadii.meaning: 对远方的人或事物的思念
semanticRadii.example: His letters were filled with yearning for his family.

semanticRadii.label: 抽象向往
semanticRadii.example: There was a yearning in her voice to be understood.

semanticRadii.label: 文学/正式用语
semanticRadii.example: The poem captures the universal yearning for freedom.

grammarRules.title: 语法结构
items: yearning for sth——最常见的搭配，表达对某物的渴望。a yearning to do sth——渴望做某事。常见修饰语：deep/intense/desperate yearning。常与heart/soul/voice搭配，表达从内心深处发出的渴望。

exampleDiagnoses.example: He spoke of his homeland with a yearning that bordered on physical pain.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 思念具身化——想家想到身体都疼，这是yearning的极致。

exampleDiagnoses.example: Every creative act begins with a yearning to make the world different.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 创造动力——艺术的源头从来不是技巧，是向往。

synonymComparisons.difference: 持久的、情感深层的向往（温柔）
synonymComparisons.example: She gazed at the photo with undisguised yearning.

synonymComparisons.difference: 强烈的、带有痛苦的渴望（更强烈）
synonymComparisons.example: He was consumed by a longing to return home.

synonymComparisons.difference: 生理冲动式的渴望（更具体）
synonymComparisons.example: She had a sudden craving for chocolate.

synonymComparisons.difference: 最中性的欲望/愿望（范围最广）
synonymComparisons.example: Desire is the root of all ambition.

oneLinePenetration: yearning是渴望家族中最温柔的一个。longing灼烧你，craving折磨你，desire驱动你——但yearning只是安静地待在你心里，偶尔抬头看向远方。它不是你需要被满足的东西，它是你之所以为你的证据。

forms.note: 易弯曲的；让步的；柔顺的
不屈的；坚硬的；不让步的

coreImage: 你在高速公路上开到岔路口，看到YIELD标志——没有警察逼你停，但你知道：你得让对方先走。这不是认输，是明知道可以争、却选择把优先权交出去。农人说这块田今年yield了800斤——土地让出了它的成果。而一位母亲对哭闹的孩子yield了——她不是被说服了，是判断坚持的代价太高。yield的智慧：有时退一步，是给更大的事物让出空间。

semanticRadii.label: 让步/屈服
semanticRadii.example: He finally yielded to his family's demands and took the job.

semanticRadii.label: 交通用语
semanticRadii.example: Drivers must yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.

semanticRadii.label: 农业/金融
semanticRadii.example: The bond offers a yield of 4.5% per annum.

grammarRules.title: 用法规则
items: yield to sth/sb——屈服于/to不能省略。yield + 名词（产出结果）：yield information/clues/results/dividends。yield the floor/the right of way——正式场合用语。名词后of：a yield of…（…的产量/收益率）。

exampleDiagnoses.example: She refused to yield to fear and delivered the speech despite her trembling hands.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 意志力——颤抖着前进，就是没有屈服。

exampleDiagnoses.example: The apple trees yield their best fruit only after a cold winter.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 自然哲理——没有寒冷，就没有最甜的果实。

synonymComparisons.difference: 在压力下让步/有产出（双向含义）
synonymComparisons.example: The government yielded to public pressure.

synonymComparisons.difference: 完全放弃抵抗（军事/情感投降）
synonymComparisons.example: The army surrendered after a three-week siege.

synonymComparisons.difference: 服从权威/更高力量（偏向臣服）
synonymComparisons.example: She refused to submit to his control.

synonymComparisons.difference: 制造/产出（纯动作，不含让步）
synonymComparisons.example: The factory produces 500 cars a day.

oneLinePenetration: yield的双面性——创造和放弃共享同一个动词。你让出道路(向他人yield)，土地让出果实(大自然yields)。最深刻的学习者懂得：真正的yield不是懦弱——是判断哪些仗值得打。向真理yield，向爱yield，向更好的自己yield——这不是输，这是让更值得的事物占据你。

forms.note: 分区制；区域规划（尤指城市规划）

coreImage: 站在机场出发大厅，头顶挂着蓝底白字：DEPARTURE ZONE。你跨过地上那条线，空间没有变，但意义变了——你不再是在里面混日子的那个人，你是即将起飞的人。zone不是物理空间本身，是人给空间划的那条边界。当你进入一个zone，规则改变、身份改变、你的行为方式也该改变。舒适区是zone，战区也是zone——空间的本质是人赋予它的约束和许可。

semanticRadii.label: 抽象区间
semanticRadii.example: Stepping out of your comfort zone is how you grow.

semanticRadii.label: 动作"进入状态"
semanticRadii.example: I just zoned out during the entire meeting.

semanticRadii.label: 规划分区
semanticRadii.example: The land is zoned for residential development.

grammarRules.title: 语法结构
items: in/out of the zone——进入/脱离专注状态。zone out——走神；发呆。zone in (on sth)——集中注意力/锁定目标。used as countable noun——最常见的用法。搭配：comfort/war/buffer/no-fly/time zone等。

exampleDiagnoses.example: The buffer zone between the two countries has been peaceful for decades.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 物理边界——线的意义不是分隔，是保护。

exampleDiagnoses.example: You'll never know what you're capable of until you leave your comfort zone.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 成长哲理——边界存在就是为了被跨越。

synonymComparisons.difference: 有明确边界或功能定义的区域
synonymComparisons.example: No smoking in this zone.

synonymComparisons.difference: 中性泛指任何地域（最宽泛）
synonymComparisons.example: This area is known for its vineyards.

synonymComparisons.difference: 自然或行政意义上的大区域
synonymComparisons.example: The region has experienced rapid growth.

synonymComparisons.difference: 城市内有特定特征的片区
synonymComparisons.example: The financial district is always crowded.

oneLinePenetration: zone的核心是边界带来的意义转换。同一个地方，你叫它家还是一个zone，区别在于有没有一条明确的线。人生的每一次成长，本质都是把旧的zone划掉，给自己画一个新的zone。

posNote: 随意地、漫不经心地、偶然地

forms.note: 核心词性：随意地、漫不经心地、偶然地
随意的、非正式的、漫不经心的
随意、漫不经心（指态度或氛围）

coreImage:
你手里握着一张藏宝图，心里明明激动得要命，但走进人群时，你故意把图卷起来，像拿着一卷废纸那样晃荡，随口对旁边的人说："哦，这个啊，我捡来的。"

这个动作的精髓在于：用"看起来毫不费力"的方式来掩盖、或附加、或消解某件事的真实重量。它不只是"穿得随便"，而是"在故意或无意地，改变信息或行为的表面称重"。
atomicCore: 以"非紧绷、非郑重"的方式行事，使行为或信息呈现出较低的重量级。

semanticRadii.label: 半径0（外在形态）
semanticRadii.example: We are allowed to dress casually on Fridays.

semanticRadii.label: 半径1（行为姿态）
semanticRadii.example: He leaned casually against the counter.

semanticRadii.label: 半径2（信息抛出）
semanticRadii.meaning: 随口地（表面轻描淡写，但信息本身可能分量极重）
semanticRadii.example: She casually dropped the news that she was quitting.

semanticRadii.label: 半径3（注意力分配）
semanticRadii.meaning: 敷衍地（不经心地扫一眼）
semanticRadii.example: He casually scanned the contract before signing.

grammarRules.title: 副词位置
items: 动前（最标准）：She casually mentioned her promotion.
动后（强调动作）：She mentioned her promotion casually.
句首（强调态度基调）：Casually, she mentioned her promotion.

grammarRules.title: 必背搭配
items: casually dressed — 穿得休闲
casually mention / remark — 随口一提
casually glance — 随意一瞥

grammarRules.title: 核心禁忌
items: 绝不用于描述系统性的、有规律的动作（如：✘ The bus casually arrives at 8am. 因为公交到站是有规律的，不能用"随意"）

exampleDiagnoses.example: She was dressed casually, but her speech was extremely formal.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 最强反差用法。这里 casually 刻画了"外部形象"的随意，以此突出"内部表现"的严肃，形成张力。

exampleDiagnoses.example: "I'm pregnant," she said casually, as if she was talking about the weather.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 顶级用法。用 casually 来制造巨大的信息反差——内容是震撼的，但包装是轻巧的。这往往是一种防御机制。

exampleDiagnoses.example: The policeman casually walked past the suspect, then suddenly turned around.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 此处 casually 是伪装。它描述了一种刻意伪装的"正常走路"，目的是为了不惊动对方。

synonymComparisons.difference: 涉及"外表与实际不符"（可能故意，也可能只是放松）
synonymComparisons.example: She casually mentioned his name.

synonymComparisons.difference: 纯数学或程序化的"无目的"，不涉及情绪或伪装
synonymComparisons.example: The computer selected a number randomly.

synonymComparisons.difference: 纯粹"非故意"，由错误或巧合引起
synonymComparisons.example: I accidentally mentioned his name.

synonymComparisons.difference: 疏忽、不负责任，往往导致损失
synonymComparisons.example: He carelessly drove into the wall.

synonymComparisons.difference: 指社交规矩或流程不严格，不关乎"态度伪装"
synonymComparisons.example: We chatted informally over coffee.

oneLinePenetration: casually 的本质是 "行为方式的低烈度包装"。它主要修饰的不是你"做了什么"，而是你"做这件事时脸上挂着的那个表情"。它的精髓在于，你可以用"随便"的外壳，来发射一颗"认真"的子弹。

posNote: 促使、推动、引起（兼形容词、名词）
coreImage:
你走进厨房看见热水壶烧开了，你还没出声，旁边的人已经拎起水壶帮你倒了水。

prompt 的"快"不是单纯的"速度快"，而是 "在恰当的节点做出符合期待的反应"。动词指"触发这个动作的那一下推手"，形容词指"那一推几乎没有延迟"。
atomicCore: 在时间窗口内做出恰当的、合乎期待的反应或触发。

semanticRadii.label: 半径0（动词——触发行为）
semanticRadii.example: The incident prompted him to resign.

semanticRadii.label: 半径0（形容词——速度）
semanticRadii.example: Thank you for your prompt reply.

semanticRadii.label: 半径1（名词——输入提示）
semanticRadii.example: Enter your name in the prompt.

grammarRules.title: 动词结构（最重要）
items: prompt + 宾语 + to do（极常用）

grammarRules.title: 形容词用法
items: 仅作定语或表语，后不接介词
be prompt in doing — 做……很利落

grammarRules.title: 名词用法
items: 常与 for 搭配，或用于界面语境

exampleDiagnoses.example: The manager's email prompted me to reply immediately.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: prompt 作动词，强调"外部信息触发了内部动作"。

exampleDiagnoses.example: We need a prompt response before 5 p.m.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 形容词义：不只是"快"，是在"合适的时间点出现"。

exampleDiagnoses.example: The AI model gave me a text prompt.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 名词义：提示信息，强调"等待被触发"。

synonymComparisons.difference: 速度快，且切中需求点，不拖沓
synonymComparisons.example: Prompt payment.

synonymComparisons.difference: 零延迟，更强调"没有间隔"
synonymComparisons.example: Immediate danger.

synonymComparisons.difference: 速度快，但不一定踩在点上，可能只是匆忙
synonymComparisons.example: A quick reply.

oneLinePenetration: prompt = 用最短的间距，正好踩在你期待的时间点上。

forms.note: 核心词性：严厉的、刺耳的、严酷的（让人感到粗糙、不留缓冲）

coreImage:
冬天里，一阵风刮过来，不是温柔的冷，是刀子一样的、直往骨缝里钻的硬冷——空气本身像是长了倒刺。

harsh 描述的永远是 "没有柔软包边、没有缓冲层的直接接触"。它可以是声音、话语、环境或现实，共同点是它们都"不留余地"。
atomicCore: 以粗糙、尖锐或不留余地的特性给感官或心理带来不适。

semanticRadii.label: 半径0（话语/评判）
semanticRadii.meaning: 严厉的、苛刻的（不留情面）
semanticRadii.example: He received harsh criticism.

semanticRadii.label: 半径1（环境/条件）
semanticRadii.meaning: 严酷的、恶劣的（生存难度大）
semanticRadii.example: A harsh winter killed the crops.

semanticRadii.label: 半径2（感官/声音/光）
semanticRadii.example: The harsh light hurt my eyes.

grammarRules.title: 语法位置
items: 可作定语/表语：a harsh voice（定语），The conditions are harsh（表语）
常用加强词：extremely harsh、too harsh

grammarRules.title: 固定介词搭配
items: harsh on + 人/事物 — "对……很苛刻"

exampleDiagnoses.example: His teacher's words were harsh, but they woke him up.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 表现 harsh 的辩证面——它可以不友好，但未必无效。

exampleDiagnoses.example: The desert has one of the harshest climates on earth.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 不是"不舒服"，是"会致死"的那种严酷。

exampleDiagnoses.example: She spoke in a harsh tone that made me shrink.
exampleDiagnoses.diagnosis: 物理意义上的"刮伤"，耳朵和情绪同时被攻击。

synonymComparisons.difference: 没有包边、没有缓冲，直接作用于感官或心理
synonymComparisons.example: Harsh lighting.

synonymComparisons.difference: 有标准和规则，可能是公平的，不一定带来不适
synonymComparisons.example: Strict parents.

synonymComparisons.difference: 表面粗糙，多指物理触感，也可能指"粗略"
synonymComparisons.example: Rough hands.

synonymComparisons.difference: 程度严重，多指客观的、可测量的重
synonymComparisons.example: Severe injury.

oneLinePenetration: harsh = 没有柔光滤镜的现实，直接裸传给感官，让你知道什么叫做"不带情面的硬碰硬"。
